title: The evidence-first campaign: 50 experiments, 10 datasets x 5 stages
request: Run about 50 experiments on real public data that teach the workflow of building a model, not a leaderboard: understanding the data, finding leaks, feature engineering, choosing the algorithm and optimizing, with an LLM helping as a critic. Collect the claims so people and a future model can learn from them.
spec: Exactly 50 experiments: 10 UCI datasets x 5 stages (data understanding, leakage audit, feature engineering ablation, algorithm screen, optimization with calibration and one final holdout). Every selection on training-only CV; the locked holdout read once per dataset. Each result JSON holds evidence, claims, limitations and provenance; a manifest, a report, claim-level agent memory and an LLM review queue are generated.
plan: Write the manifest first: for each experiment its question, hypothesis, dataset and source.
Lock a holdout per dataset before any analysis; cap each table at 4,000 rows for the first pass with 3-fold stratified CV.
Stage 1: profile training rows only (missingness, duplicates, positive rate, random-split PSI as a smoke check).
Stage 2: declare decision-time exclusions (bank duration, shoppers PageValues), run heuristic proxy checks and a synthetic canary, and measure safe vs unsafe CV.
Stage 3: compare the feature ladder (raw, logs, ratios, interactions, full, selected) with folds-fitted features; pick the smallest matrix within 0.002 ROC-AUC of the best.
Stage 4: screen five families on identical folds, ranked by mean minus 0.25 x fold std.
Stage 5: try three explicit candidates for the chosen family, accept only a declared CV margin, fit once on all training rows and score the holdout once with a bootstrap interval, Brier and ECE.
Generate the report, the claims memory and 50 bounded critic tasks.

decisions.decision: The LLM is a critic and hypothesis generator only.
decisions.why: Deterministic code owns metrics, splits, provenance and evidence; a human owns ambiguous decision-time semantics and promotion.

decisions.decision: Prefer the smallest feature matrix within 0.002 of the best CV score.
decisions.why: It makes feature dilution a first-class negative result instead of rewarding every extra column.

decisions.decision: Rank model families by mean minus 0.25 x fold std, then tune only the chosen family.
decisions.why: Stability matters as much as the mean; tuning every family multiplies selection on the same folds.

decisions.decision: Treat leakage heuristics as review requests and include a synthetic canary.
decisions.why: A heuristic flag is not proof of a leak, and a detector must show it can catch an exact-target canary before its silence means anything.

change: dclab_rnd/science.py (stages) and dclab_rnd/campaign.py (orchestration, resumable run, status, verify), 50 result files under evidence/campaigns/model_building_50_v1/results/, manifest.json, CAMPAIGN_REPORT.md, AGENT_CONTEXT.md, MODEL_BUILDING_WORKFLOW.md, agent_memory.jsonl and llm_review_queue.jsonl.

findings.defect: Two derived feature recipes were selected through arithmetic on factorized category codes.
findings.scenario: bank_marketing selected `ratios` (+0.0042 over raw) and german_credit `interactions` (+0.0073); the cached tables store categories as codes in order of first appearance (May=0, Jun=1), and EXP-010's top features were poutcome, log1p_poutcome, month and log1p_month. Over 9 folds the same lifts were +0.0012 [-0.019, +0.021] and +0.0006 [-0.030, +0.031]: fold noise.
findings.cause: The earlier downloader factorized categoricals, and the feature ladder treated every numeric column as a quantity.
findings.fix: The results stay immutable; evidence/README.md lists every affected record, codes are now kept out of derived features, and category_codes_v1 measured the alternatives (see RD-category-codes).

measurements.name: leakage audit, safe vs unsafe training CV
measurements.gate: Declared decision-time exclusions are removed; the apparent lift is unsafe minus safe CV ROC-AUC, measured on training folds only.
measurements.result: bank_marketing duration: 0.7130 safe vs 0.8972 unsafe (+0.1842); online_shoppers PageValues: 0.7156 vs 0.9124 (+0.1968). The detector canary was caught on all 10 datasets.
measurements.next: Confirm the decision-time meaning of each flagged column with a domain source; a lift shows severity, not proof.

measurements.name: feature ladder selection
measurements.gate: Smallest matrix within 0.002 mean CV ROC-AUC of the best stage.
measurements.result: raw on 7 of 10 datasets; ratios on bank_marketing (+0.0042) and wine_quality (+0.0031); interactions on german_credit (+0.0073).
measurements.next: Rerun close decisions with repeated 5x5 CV and all available rows.

measurements.name: final holdout, read once per dataset
measurements.gate: Model and settings locked on training CV; a tuned candidate accepted only above the declared margin; holdout scored once with a bootstrap 95% interval.
measurements.next: Calibration review for heart_disease; thresholds from out-of-fold predictions with a cost matrix; subgroup reviews for credit and health data.

outcome: 50 of 50 experiments completed, 0 failed, every holdout read once. The campaign became the answer key for the copilot, the agent tools and the SFT corpus. Its limits are written into the report: 4,000 rows and 3 folds per dataset, factorized categoricals, and no temporal or out-of-domain holdout.
lessons: Write the question and hypothesis of every experiment before running it; the manifest is what makes 50 runs a study rather than a pile.
There was no universal best algorithm and raw features were enough on most datasets; both are defaults to challenge, not laws.
Three folds are too few to choose between recipes 0.004 apart; a later 9-fold rerun showed those wins were noise.
